samples.identification: StormAttack DLL injector/persistence loader with zeroed resources
samples.marker_content: StormAttack injector: persistence and self-delete; add service coverage
evidence: Rizin: entry 0x402674 reaches dispatch 0x401cb0. DWORD at file 0x4120 is 3: Active Setup branch 0x401f75 calls 0x401900, then shell self-delete helper 0x401390.

0x401900 creates an HKLM Active Setup Installed Components GUID key and writes a copied image path as REG_EXPAND_SZ StubPath at 0x401a4b. It reads its own image, patches configuration, writes a copy, and launches it at 0x401b7e.
Cleanup resolves its own module short path and COMSPEC, constructs /c del <self> > nul, starts it using CreateProcessA at 0x4014b8, and resumes the thread.
Alternate mode 1 extracts DLL resource 101 through 0x402460/0x4023c0. 0x401260 opens LanmanServer Parameters, deletes ServiceDLL, and writes a replacement at 0x40133e.

0x401150 creates a configured target process (IE, notepad, or calc), allocates remote memory and copies the DLL path, resolves Kernel32!LoadLibraryA, and uses it with the remote buffer in CreateRemoteThread at 0x40123d.

Previously uncovered mode 2: 0x401fd0 copies its module, sets Hidden|System attributes at 0x402181, creates an own-process auto-start executable service at 0x4021de, and starts it. Service routine 0x401510 hands an extracted DLL to the injector. This is distinct from existing ServiceDLL replacement detection.

Entire resource section at file 0x5000..0xf000 is zero-filled, and bound IAT bytes are damaged/overwritten. No intact embedded payload, functional ransomware, encryption or successful DDoS is established. Surviving persistence, execution-transfer and self-deletion code establishes malicious design.
Percent-decoded strings come from printf GUID formats, not hidden URLs or an encoded executable stage. The supplied tria.ge report was inaccessible; it did not supply verdict evidence.

samples.marker_content: SwalidJS 1.0.7: bundled code disables input and forces remote audio
evidence: First-party src/index.js is a local form validator using SweetAlert popups; manifest 1.0.7 has no install lifecycle payload. The browser bundle initializes SweetAlert2 before exposing window.Swalid.

Module-level routine tests Russian browser language and location.host for .ru/.su/.by/.xn--p1ai. It stores first-use time in localStorage. After strictly more than three days it disables body pointerEvents, appends looping remote MP3 audio, and attempts playback. Input blocking precedes and survives playback rejection.

Bundled source-map sourcesContent[0] matches byte-for-byte the canonical package/dist/sweetalert2.all.js fetched with Forager pkg:npm/sweetalert2@11.17.2. This is an actual dependency-borne sabotage routine, not evidence of a Swalid-specific injected patch.

Both isolated atomscan PURL scans preserve every dependency finding and score. Existing canonical-package disclosure downgrades its routine finding to suspicious; the undisclosed consuming bundle retains its hostile findings. No dependent-only exclusion was added.

The exact 519-character bundle conditional was evaluated with inert DOM, storage, clock, timers and audio stubs in JavaScriptCore. All eight cases passed, including elapsed-time boundaries, other language/domain, Belarus and host port. No full library, network request, audio playback or native sample was run.

Three root hostile traits cover one sabotage routine plus identity/distribution context. Source, source-map, module initialization, networking, storage and callback review found no additional theft, persistence, native execution or executable payload stage. No duplicate or invented hostile behavior was added to reach a quota.

samples.marker_content: WSO2 Carbon 4.10.41: verified upstream server; add JSP Base64 coverage
evidence: Forager fetched pkg:golang/github.com/wso2/carbon-kernel@v4.10.41+incompatible through proxy.golang.org and verified module h1:aQrbLBkLkFT9/+Id4QW5V8xC3I1p3dvF7l5DX8Fd7+4= against sum.golang.org. Recovered ZIP is byte-identical to the supplied SHA256 d68e2ed9d3e91819bc437254dcb283398591faa5451d21ccfe7a8b17272cf4b4.

README, Maven POM and implementation agree on an OSGi middleware/server framework. Review covered launcher, startup scripts, upload routing, JSP SOAP proxy, configured crypto providers and the heavily flagged vendored JS.

Main.writePID invokes sh -c echo $PPID and writes wso2carbon.pid. SystemValidator invokes bash -c ulimit -n to check startup resources; integration tests start/stop local servers. These purposeful operations remain detected.

SymmetricEncryption and KeyStoreBasedExternalCryptoProvider initialize configured encryption/decryption for application/configuration data. CipherHolder and registry synchronization use Base64 for data representation. No victim-file encryption or secret exfiltration chain was established.

Prototype evalResponse is controlled by evalJS, same-origin and content-type checks unless the caller explicitly forces it. jQuery script-node execution is part of its documented API implementation. The reviewed minified libraries/encoded vectors match their upstream/test roles.

WSRequestXSSproxy_ajaxprocessor.jsp decodes Base64 input strings, configures secured XML parsing, and invokes Axis2 SOAP handling. Existing JVM Base64.decode rule omitted JSP; extending that scope adds exactly one notable member finding and preserves Java/Kotlin scope.

Zero hostile/suspicious findings is not the verdict rationale: purposeful source behavior and checksum-verified provenance tip the balance. Deployment configuration and evidence about any particular running server were not supplied. No package exception or accurate dual-use detection was removed.
